question.prompt: How many two-digit positive integers have at least one \(7\) as a digit?

solutions.explanation:
A two-digit number containing a \(7\) must have it in the tens place or the ones place. There are \(10\) numbers with tens digit \(7\), namely \(70\) through \(79\). There are \(9\) two-digit numbers ending in \(7\), namely \(17,27,\ldots,97\).

These groups include every eligible number, but \(77\) appears in both. It is the only overlap, so subtract one copy:
\[10+9-1=\boxed{18}.\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Count the two digit positions
